channel.title: Muhammad Jahanzaib Awan — Writing
channel.description: Short technical posts on machine learning, evaluation and data science.

item.title: Data Science Degrees vs Portfolios: What Interviews Check
item.description: Degrees and portfolios both signal something, but interviews test neither directly. Here is what actually gets checked.

item.title: How to Read a Confusion Matrix Class by Class
item.description: A model with 94% accuracy can still be useless for the one class you care about. Learn to read confusion matrices row by row, not just the headline number.

item.title: Computer Vision Syndrome vs Evaluating Computer Vision Models
item.description: Computer vision syndrome is eye strain from screens. Model evaluation is how we judge vision systems. Same name, nothing else in common, and the confusion teaches a lesson about precision.

item.title: The Prompt Engineering Skill Set: What Transfers
item.description: Prompt tricks age fast, but the underlying skills of decomposition, evaluation and constraint design do not. Here is how to tell the difference.

item.title: MLOps Tools Compared: Ten Users Versus Ten Thousand
item.description: Most MLOps advice is written for scale you don't have yet. Here's a leakage-aware, honest guide to what to adopt at ten users versus ten thousand.

item.title: Positional Encodings: Why Transformers Need Them at All
item.description: Self-attention is permutation-invariant by default. Without positional encodings, a transformer literally cannot tell 'dog bites man' from 'man bites dog'.

item.title: Sequence Labelling Metrics: Why Token Accuracy Lies
item.description: High token accuracy on sequence labelling tasks can mask a much worse entity-level error rate. Here's the arithmetic that proves it.

item.title: Domain Adaptation Versus Fine-Tuning: Adapting Is Not Retraining
item.description: Fine-tuning a model on new data is not the same as adapting it to a new domain. The difference decides whether your reported gains survive contact with reality.

item.title: Building a Minimal Model Card Before Anyone Uses Your Model
item.description: Before anyone downloads your model, tell them what it was trained on, how it was evaluated, and where it breaks. Here is the minimal version that actually gets written.

item.title: The Actual Skills That Get You Hired as an ML Engineer
item.description: Hiring for ML engineering rewards rigorous evaluation and shipping discipline, not the fanciest model architecture on your CV.

item.title: Fine-Tuning vs Few-Shot Prompting on Small Datasets
item.description: With small labelled datasets, fine-tuning and few-shot prompting fail differently. Here's how to choose, and how to evaluate the choice honestly.

item.title: Macro, Micro, and Weighted Averages Explained Properly
item.description: Accuracy lies when classes are imbalanced. I walk through macro, micro, and weighted F1 with real numbers so you know which one to trust.

item.title: Choosing a Pretrained Transformer: Size, Licence, Context
item.description: Model choice is a systems decision, not a leaderboard lookup. Here is how size, licence, and context length interact in practice.

item.title: Cross-Validation Folds for Grouped Data: Silent Leakage
item.description: Random folds leak when data has groups: patients, users, sessions. Here's why the fix is grouped splitting, not more data.

item.title: What a Machine Learning Engineer's Week Actually Looks Like
item.description: The job is less 'train a model' and more data cleaning, evaluation design, and stopping silent failures before they reach production.

item.title: NLP Techniques Before Deep Learning: A Practical Refresher
item.description: Classic NLP methods still catch leakage, expose weak baselines and explain model behaviour better than most deep nets ever will.

item.title: Designing an Evaluation Harness Before You Know the Job
item.description: A practical guide to building leakage-aware, adaptable evaluation harnesses for models whose final job is not yet fully defined.

item.title: Model Evaluation for Extreme Risks: What Red-Teaming Tests
item.description: Red-teaming finds failures; it does not bound risk. Here is what it actually measures, with a worked example showing why absence of evidence is not evidence of absence.

item.title: The Transformer Architecture, Explained Without the Maths
item.description: A no-equations tour of transformers: what attention actually does, why position matters, and why the architecture scaled so well.

item.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: What Actually Gets Updated
item.description: A worked look at how adapters and LoRA fine-tune large models by updating a small slice of parameters, and why that matters for real projects.
